# Lab 6.4: Clustering

## What We Are Going to Do
Cluster a table on up to four columns, see block pruning in bytes processed, and check that BigQuery re-clusters automatically.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a partitioned and clustered table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab06.trips_clustered
PARTITION BY DATE(trip_start_timestamp)
CLUSTER BY company, payment_type
AS SELECT * FROM lab06.trips_flat;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Compare a filter on the cluster column.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(fare) FROM lab06.trips_daily
WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) BETWEEN '2023-06-01' AND '2023-06-30' AND company = 'Flash Cab';

SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(fare) FROM lab06.trips_clustered
WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) BETWEEN '2023-06-01' AND '2023-06-30' AND company = 'Flash Cab';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The clustered table reads fewer bytes. Note the dry-run estimate is the same for both: clustering savings appear only after the query runs.

3. **[SQL] Column order matters.** Filter on the second column only:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab06.trips_clustered
WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '2023-06-15' AND payment_type = 'Cash';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Pruning is weaker, because data is sorted by `company` first.

4. **[CLI] Change clustering on an existing table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq update --clustering_fields=company,payment_type,taxi_id lab06.trips_clustered
bq show --format=prettyjson lab06.trips_clustered | grep -A5 clustering</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   New data uses the new clustering. BigQuery re-clusters in the background for free.

5. **[Console] Check the details.** Open `trips_clustered → Details`. See **Clustered by** and **Partitioned by**.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Cluster columns | Up to 4, order matters |
| Bytes billed | Lower after the query runs |
| Dry run | Does not show clustering savings |
| Re-clustering | Automatic and free |
